Gene Description

Pax6 is a paired-box/paired-type homeobox transcription factor that binds DNA through an N-terminal bipartite paired domain (PAI and RED subdomains) and a C-terminal homeodomain, and activates or represses RNA polymerase II target genes via a C-terminal proline/serine/threonine-rich transactivation domain. Alternative splicing produces the canonical protein, the Pax6(5a) isoform with an altered paired domain, and a paired-less p32 isoform. Pax6 is a dosage-sensitive master regulator of eye development: it is required in head surface ectoderm for lens placode formation and lens development, in the optic cup for retinal progenitor and retinal pigment epithelium specification, and for cornea, iris and lacrimal gland development; heterozygous Small eye (Sey) mice model human aniridia. In the central nervous system it patterns the dorsal telencephalon (pallium) and pallial/subpallial boundary, sets rostrolateral cortical area identity, drives cortical radial glia neurogenesis through a Pax6-Eomes/Tbr2-Tbr1 cascade while restraining progenitor proliferation, establishes ventral progenitor domains in spinal cord and hindbrain in response to graded Shh, and contributes to diencephalic, cerebellar and olfactory development. In the pancreas Pax6 is required for endocrine (especially glucagon-producing alpha and insulin-producing beta) cell differentiation and directly activates proglucagon, MafB, cMaf and NeuroD1. Its activity is modulated by HIPK2 phosphorylation and p300 binding, SUMOylation, TRIM11-mediated degradation, and interaction with Smad3, Sox and Groucho-family partners.

Core Functions

Pax6 is a sequence-specific RNA polymerase II transcription factor that binds promoter/enhancer elements of eye, CNS and pancreatic-endocrine target genes through its paired domain and homeodomain and activates their transcription.

Molecular Function:
DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific
Directly Involved In:
positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
Cellular Locations:
chromatin nucleus
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:20592023
    Pax6 directly binds and activates the promoter region of the three genes through specific binding sites
  • PMID:12756174
    both, Pax2 and Pax6 bind to and activate a MITF RPE-promoter element in vitro
  • PMID:19521500
    finding that Pax6 positively and directly regulates cohorts of genes that promote neural stem cell self-renewal, basal progenitor cell genesis, and neurogenesis

In a context-dependent manner Pax6 acts as a sequence-specific transcriptional repressor, e.g. of cell-cycle genes such as Cdk6 in cortical progenitors and of Trap (with the Groucho corepressor Grg6) in osteoclast precursors.

Molecular Function:
DNA-binding transcription repressor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific
Directly Involved In:
negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
Cellular Locations:
chromatin
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:23622063
    Biochemical assays indicated that Pax6 directly represses Cdk6 expression
  • PMID:23990468
    Pax6 binds endogenously to the proximal region of the tartrate acid phosphatase (TRAP) gene promoter and suppresses nuclear factor of activated T cells c1 (NFATc1)-induced TRAP gene expression

Pax6 transcriptional output is tuned by binding of coregulators and signalling effectors: the HAT coactivator p300 (enhanced by HIPK2 phosphorylation), the R-SMAD Smad3 (via the paired-domain RED subdomain), Sox HMG-box partners and Groucho-family corepressors.

Molecular Function:
transcription coregulator binding
Directly Involved In:
regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
Cellular Locations:
nucleus
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:16407227
    HIPK2 phosphorylates the activation domain of Pax6, which augments Pax6 transactivation by enhancing its interaction with p300
  • PMID:17251190
    the MH1 domain of Smad3 was observed binding the RED sub-domain of the Pax6 paired domain

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Do the canonical Pax6 and Pax6(5a) isoforms bind distinct target repertoires in vivo (paired domain PAI vs RED usage), and does this explain the proliferation-versus-fate split seen in retroviral overexpression?

Q: Several MGI experimental annotations (chromatin binding PMID:23637604; negative regulation of protein phosphorylation PMID:16497297; signal transduction PMID:18462699) cite papers whose available text does not mention Pax6. Can MGI confirm the intended references?

Q: Should the GO-level role of Pax6 in Shh-patterned neural tube be represented as a Shh-responsive transcriptional target (has-input/causal relation in GO-CAM) rather than as participation in smoothened signaling?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Allelic series (Sey/+, wild type, PAX77 overexpression) combined with CUT&RUN for Pax6 and chromatin accessibility in lens placode and E12.5 cortical radial glia to relate binding-site affinity to dosage-dependent target expression.

Hypothesis: Pax6 dosage sensitivity in lens and cortex reflects concentration-dependent occupancy of low-affinity enhancers.

Experiment: Isoform-specific knock-in mice lacking p32 initiation or the K91 SUMO site, followed by RNA-seq and homeodomain-site ChIP in retina and olfactory bulb.

Hypothesis: The paired-less p32 isoform has distinct, SUMO-dependent homeodomain-only targets in eye and olfactory bulb.

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(Pax6-notes.md)

Pax6 (mouse, P63015) curation notes

Provenance / method

  • Automated deep research was NOT available for this gene (falcon provider returned HTTP 402, OpenAI 401).
    No -deep-research-<provider>.md file was created. These notes were assembled manually from the cached
    publications in publications/, the UniProt record (Pax6-uniprot.txt) and the completed human
    ortholog review (genes/human/PAX6/PAX6-ai-review.yaml).
  • Many cited MGI papers are abstract-only in the cache; for those, the "do not overrule curators" rule was
    applied (developmental IMP rows kept as non-core; UNDECIDED where the abstract does not mention Pax6).

Molecular function

  • Paired-box family TF; paired domain sufficient for sequence-specific DNA binding
    PMID:10197584.
  • Direct target activation: Mitf RPE promoter PMID:12756174;
    alpha-cell genes MafB, cMaf, NeuroD1 PMID:20592023;
    Sox2 PMID:18287938;
    Six6 with Lhx2 PMID:19146846.
  • Genome-wide cortical targets PMID:19521500;
    Pax6-Tbr2-Tbr1 cascade PMID:30186101.
  • Repressor activity: PMID:23622063;
    Trap/Acp5 in osteoclast lineage PMID:23990468
    with Grg6/Tle6 PMID:23990468.
  • Regulation of Pax6 activity: HIPK2/p300 PMID:16407227;
    Smad3 PMID:17251190 -- NOTE the same paper
    invalidates Smad4 binding PMID:17251190
    -> co-SMAD binding (GO:0070410) REMOVED (human review had accepted an IEA co-SMAD row; disagreement noted);
    Trim11 degradation PMID:18628401;
    SUMOylation of p32 isoform PMID:21084637;
    lncRNA Paupar PMID:24488179.

Isoforms

  • Pax6(5a) vs canonical paired domain PMID:15548580;
    PD essential in brain PMID:15548580.
  • Paired-less isoform PMID:16464444.

Biological roles (mostly non-core, KEEP_AS_NON_CORE)

  • Eye: lens placode PMID:11069887;
    cornea PMID:16080917;
    lacrimal gland PMID:10821755.
  • Telencephalon: PMID:11050125;
    PMID:15878992.
  • Spinal cord/hindbrain: PMID:9230312.
  • Pancreas: PMID:20592023.

Problem annotations

  • GO:0003682 chromatin binding IDA PMID:23637604: cached full text is a Candida albicans/Dectin-1 paper with no Pax6 mention -> UNDECIDED, reference flagged WRONG_IDENTIFIER.
  • GO:0001933 (PMID:16497297, HSP27), GO:0023019 (PMID:18462699, ER71), GO:0007224 (PMID:18590716, FKBP8), GO:0045665 (PMID:16950124),
    GO:0042462 (PMID:12648492): abstracts do not support the specific Pax6 claim -> UNDECIDED.
  • GO:0007601 visual perception: Pax6 Sey-Dey eyeless mice used only as blind controls -> over-annotation.
  • GO:0030216 keratinocyte differentiation -> MODIFY to GO:0160122 corneal epithelial cell differentiation.
  • protein binding rows -> REMOVE, except Tle6/Grg6 row -> MODIFY to GO:0001222 transcription corepressor binding.

id: P63015
gene_symbol: Pax6
product_type: PROTEIN
status: COMPLETE
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:10090
  label: Mus musculus
description: 'Pax6 is a paired-box/paired-type homeobox transcription factor that binds DNA through an
  N-terminal bipartite paired domain (PAI and RED subdomains) and a C-terminal homeodomain, and activates
  or represses RNA polymerase II target genes via a C-terminal proline/serine/threonine-rich transactivation
  domain. Alternative splicing produces the canonical protein, the Pax6(5a) isoform with an altered paired
  domain, and a paired-less p32 isoform. Pax6 is a dosage-sensitive master regulator of eye development:
  it is required in head surface ectoderm for lens placode formation and lens development, in the optic
  cup for retinal progenitor and retinal pigment epithelium specification, and for cornea, iris and lacrimal
  gland development; heterozygous Small eye (Sey) mice model human aniridia. In the central nervous system
  it patterns the dorsal telencephalon (pallium) and pallial/subpallial boundary, sets rostrolateral cortical
  area identity, drives cortical radial glia neurogenesis through a Pax6-Eomes/Tbr2-Tbr1 cascade while
  restraining progenitor proliferation, establishes ventral progenitor domains in spinal cord and hindbrain
  in response to graded Shh, and contributes to diencephalic, cerebellar and olfactory development. In
  the pancreas Pax6 is required for endocrine (especially glucagon-producing alpha and insulin-producing
  beta) cell differentiation and directly activates proglucagon, MafB, cMaf and NeuroD1. Its activity
  is modulated by HIPK2 phosphorylation and p300 binding, SUMOylation, TRIM11-mediated degradation, and
  interaction with Smad3, Sox and Groucho-family partners.'

- term:
    id: GO:0070410
    label: co-SMAD binding
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:17251190
  qualifier: enables
  review:
    summary: co-SMAD (Smad4) binding reported from GST pull-down.
    action: REMOVE
    reason: The cited paper itself states that the Smad4 interaction seen in GST pull-down could not be
      validated by co-immunoprecipitation and was invalidated, whereas Smad3 (R-SMAD) binding was validated.
      The co-SMAD binding claim is contradicted by the source paper; the R-SMAD binding annotation (GO:0070412)
      captures the validated interaction. The human PAX6 review removes its electronic co-SMAD row for the
      same reason, so the two reviews agree.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:17251190
      supporting_text: These data serve to validate the interaction of Smad3, and non-interaction of Smad2
        with Pax6, while invalidating the Smad4 interaction that was observed only in vitro

core_functions:
- description: Pax6 is a sequence-specific RNA polymerase II transcription factor that binds promoter/enhancer
    elements of eye, CNS and pancreatic-endocrine target genes through its paired domain and homeodomain
    and activates their transcription.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0000981
    label: DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0045944
    label: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
  locations:
  - id: GO:0000785
    label: chromatin
  - id: GO:0005634
    label: nucleus
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:20592023
    supporting_text: Pax6 directly binds and activates the promoter region of the three genes through
      specific binding sites
  - reference_id: PMID:12756174
    supporting_text: both, Pax2 and Pax6 bind to and activate a MITF RPE-promoter element in vitro
  - reference_id: PMID:19521500
    supporting_text: finding that Pax6 positively and directly regulates cohorts of genes that promote
      neural stem cell self-renewal, basal progenitor cell genesis, and neurogenesis
- description: In a context-dependent manner Pax6 acts as a sequence-specific transcriptional repressor,
    e.g. of cell-cycle genes such as Cdk6 in cortical progenitors and of Trap (with the Groucho corepressor
    Grg6) in osteoclast precursors.
  molecular_function:

    supporting_text: Biochemical assays indicated that Pax6 directly represses Cdk6 expression
  - reference_id: PMID:23990468
    supporting_text: Pax6 binds endogenously to the proximal region of the tartrate acid phosphatase (TRAP)
      gene promoter and suppresses nuclear factor of activated T cells c1 (NFATc1)-induced TRAP gene expression
- description: 'Pax6 transcriptional output is tuned by binding of coregulators and signalling effectors:
    the HAT coactivator p300 (enhanced by HIPK2 phosphorylation), the R-SMAD Smad3 (via the paired-domain
    RED subdomain), Sox HMG-box partners and Groucho-family corepressors.'

      by enhancing its interaction with p300
  - reference_id: PMID:17251190
    supporting_text: the MH1 domain of Smad3 was observed binding the RED sub-domain of the Pax6 paired

proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: Do the canonical Pax6 and Pax6(5a) isoforms bind distinct target repertoires in vivo (paired
    domain PAI vs RED usage), and does this explain the proliferation-versus-fate split seen in retroviral
    overexpression?
- question: Several MGI experimental annotations (chromatin binding PMID:23637604; negative regulation
    of protein phosphorylation PMID:16497297; signal transduction PMID:18462699) cite papers whose available
    text does not mention Pax6. Can MGI confirm the intended references?
- question: Should the GO-level role of Pax6 in Shh-patterned neural tube be represented as a Shh-responsive
    transcriptional target (has-input/causal relation in GO-CAM) rather than as participation in smoothened
    signaling?
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: Pax6 dosage sensitivity in lens and cortex reflects concentration-dependent occupancy of
    low-affinity enhancers.
  description: Allelic series (Sey/+, wild type, PAX77 overexpression) combined with CUT&RUN for Pax6
    and chromatin accessibility in lens placode and E12.5 cortical radial glia to relate binding-site
    affinity to dosage-dependent target expression.
- hypothesis: The paired-less p32 isoform has distinct, SUMO-dependent homeodomain-only targets in eye
    and olfactory bulb.
  description: Isoform-specific knock-in mice lacking p32 initiation or the K91 SUMO site, followed by
    RNA-seq and homeodomain-site ChIP in retina and olfactory bulb.
